project.name: Digital savings account onboarding (early idea)
project.description: A bank wants customers to open a savings account from the mobile app. Stakeholders have only rough ideas so far. Good for showing vague input, clarification questions and a Spiral recommendation.

documents.title: 01 Product Manager Interview
documents.masked_text:
Interviewer: What do you want to build?

Priya Menon (Product Manager): We want people to open an account on their phone, quickly, without visiting a branch. Something like a few minutes, maybe less. I'm not sure what the target should be yet. It has to feel easy and secure, and we shouldn't ask for too much. You can reach me on [EMAIL_1] or [PHONE_1] if you need more.

Interviewer: How do you verify who they are?

Priya Menon: Probably a selfie or a video call, we haven't decided. Maybe Aadhaar, maybe other documents. Risky customers should get extra checks, but I don't know how we decide who is risky. We'll figure that out with the fraud team later. If verification fails we should do something sensible, maybe let them try again, maybe send them to a person.

Interviewer: Timeline?

Priya Menon: We'd like a pilot soon, and we'll learn from it. The rules will probably change as we go, so let's not lock too much down. We need it live before the festival season if possible.

documents.title: 02 Compliance Email
documents.masked_text:
From: Arjun Rao (Compliance Officer)
To: Digital Banking Project
Subject: KYC points for the new app

Team,

Whatever we build must obviously follow the RBI KYC rules, and we must keep customer records for the required period. I think it is five years but please don't quote me. We also need some kind of consent from the customer. Screening against sanctions lists is needed too, though I haven't checked how the vendor does it.

I am not sure whether video KYC counts for these accounts or whether Aadhaar OTP is enough. The guidance seems to be moving and I can't give you a final answer yet. Let's keep the design flexible so it can change if the regulator updates anything.

Regards,
Arjun

documents.title: 03 Operations Notes
documents.masked_text:
Operations meeting notes (Neha Iyer, Operations Lead)

- Today, branch staff check documents by eye. It is slow and some mistakes get through.
- New flow should reduce manual work. We don't know yet how many cases will still need a person; maybe 10 or 20 percent, hard to say.
- Support staff will need to see the customer's documents sometimes. Unclear who should be allowed to.
- Our core banking system is old. It can probably take new accounts through an API but nobody has tested that.
- Customers who abandon halfway are a problem. We'd like them to be able to resume somehow.
- Budget is limited and leadership wants to see something working by next quarter.

controls.title: Customer identification and verification
controls.description: Regulated entities must identify every customer before establishing an account-based relationship and verify identity using an Officially Valid Document (passport, driving licence, voter ID, proof of Aadhaar possession, NREGA card) or its equivalent e-document, together with PAN or Form 60. Customers must not be allowed to open anonymous or fictitious-name accounts.

controls.title: Risk-based customer categorisation
controls.description: Each customer must be categorised as low, medium or high risk using documented parameters such as customer type, geography, product, delivery channel and transaction pattern. The intensity of due diligence and monitoring must match the assigned risk category, and the categorisation must be reviewable.

controls.title: Sanctions and watchlist screening
controls.description: Customers and related parties must be screened against applicable sanctions lists, and assets of designated persons must be frozen without delay and reported to the authorities.

controls.title: PEP identification and senior approval
controls.description: Institutions need risk-management systems to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person and, for foreign PEPs and higher-risk domestic PEPs, must obtain senior management approval, establish source of wealth and funds, and conduct enhanced ongoing monitoring.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall identify politically exposed persons during onboarding and require senior management approval before activating their accounts.

controls.title: Beneficial ownership of legal entities
controls.description: For companies, partnerships, trusts and other legal entities, the natural persons who ultimately own or control the entity must be identified and verified. A controlling ownership interest is defined by a percentage threshold set in the direction (verify the current figure); where no owner meets the threshold the person exercising control, or the senior managing official, is identified.

controls.title: Enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers
controls.description: High-risk customers, politically exposed persons and non-face-to-face customers require enhanced due diligence: additional identity evidence, source of funds or wealth where relevant, senior management approval before establishing or continuing a relationship with a PEP, and closer ongoing monitoring.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall trigger enhanced due diligence, including additional evidence and compliance approval, for customers categorised as high risk.

controls.title: Notice and consent for personal data
controls.description: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose, with free, specific, informed and unambiguous consent after a clear notice, or under a defined legitimate use such as compliance with a legal obligation. Consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give, and the data fiduciary must be able to show it was obtained.

controls.title: Data minimisation and purpose limitation
controls.description: Only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose may be collected, and it must be erased once the purpose is served unless a law requires retention. KYC records retained under anti-money-laundering law are a legal-retention case.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall collect only the identity data necessary for KYC and shall not reuse it for other purposes without separate consent.

controls.title: Record retention for at least five years
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.

controls.title: Periodic KYC refresh (re-KYC)
controls.description: KYC information must be periodically updated: at least every two years for high-risk customers, every eight years for medium-risk and every ten years for low-risk customers. Customers must be able to submit self-declarations of unchanged details, and accounts must not be closed without notice for missing updates.

controls.title: Ongoing transaction monitoring
controls.description: Transactions must be monitored on an ongoing basis against the customer's profile and risk category, with alert rules calibrated to risk, documented alert handling, and prescribed threshold reports such as large cash transactions.

controls.title: Suspicious activity reporting
controls.description: Reporting entities must report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India promptly after concluding that a transaction is suspicious (the Rules set a short working-day deadline, verify the current figure), must not tip off the customer, and must keep the reasoning for decisions not to report.

controls.title: Biometric liveness and presentation-attack detection
controls.description: Biometric capture used for identity verification should include presentation attack detection (liveness) that is tested against spoofing with photos, replayed video, masks and deepfakes, and report attack-detection error rates.

controls.title: Document authenticity and tamper detection
controls.description: Identity assurance level 2 requires evidence of identity to be validated as genuine and the applicant to be verified as its owner, in person or remotely, using biometric comparison or equivalent, with detection of forged or tampered documents and presentation attacks.

controls.title: Central KYC registry integration
controls.description: Regulated entities must upload customer KYC records to the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) within the prescribed period after onboarding, generate or use the KYC identifier, and fetch existing records from the registry before asking the customer to resubmit documents.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall look up existing records in the central KYC registry before requesting documents and upload new KYC records within the prescribed period.

controls.title: Tamper-evident audit trail of KYC decisions
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall keep a tamper-evident audit trail of every KYC decision, override and data access, recording who acted, when, and why.

controls.title: Encryption and masking of KYC data
controls.description: The data fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including data processed by processors, by taking reasonable security safeguards such as encryption, obfuscation or masking, access controls and logging, to prevent a personal data breach.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall encrypt KYC data in transit and at rest and mask identifiers such as Aadhaar and PAN wherever they are displayed or logged.

controls.title: Role-based access to KYC data
controls.description: An information security management system should apply controls for access management and least privilege, cryptography, logging and monitoring, secure development, supplier relationships and incident management.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall restrict access to KYC records by role on a least-privilege basis and log every access to full identity documents.

controls.title: Breach detection and notification
controls.description: On a personal data breach the data fiduciary must notify the Data Protection Board and each affected data principal in the prescribed form and manner.

controls.title: Data-subject rights handling
controls.description: Data principals have the right to access a summary of their data and processing, to correct and complete it, to request erasure (subject to legal retention), to grievance redress, and to nominate another person to exercise rights.

controls.title: Manual review and appeal of automated decisions
controls.description: People have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, such as automatically rejecting an account application. Where such decisions are permitted, safeguards include the right to human intervention, to express a view and to contest the decision.

threats.threat: Deepfake or pre-recorded video used to bypass selfie verification.
Modification of risk assessment scores to bypass AML screening.
Customer denies initiating an account opening request.
Unauthorized access to stored identity documents by internal staff.
API flooding to prevent legitimate customers from completing onboarding.
Support staff accessing administrative functions to alter KYC status.
Leaking of PII through insecure API responses to the core banking system.
Forged identity documents submitted during the onboarding process.

risks.risk: Insecure mobile implementation could lead to account takeover or unauthorized access.
risks.mitigation: Implement certificate pinning and secure storage for session tokens.

risks.risk: Remote account opening increases the risk of identity fraud if verification is not robust.
risks.mitigation: Mandate multi-factor authentication and liveness detection for all remote sessions.

risks.risk: Vague security requirements lead to inconsistent implementation, creating exploitable vulnerabilities.
risks.mitigation: Define specific security controls based on OWASP ASVS Level 2.

risks.risk: Lack of standardized verification protocols may result in accepting fraudulent documents.
risks.mitigation: Define specific technical standards for document validation and biometric matching.

risks.risk: Failure to define 'risky' customers leads to inconsistent EDD, causing regulatory non-compliance.
risks.mitigation: Establish a clear, rule-based risk scoring matrix for customer categorization.

risks.risk: Poorly defined escalation paths result in high customer abandonment or manual processing bottlenecks.
risks.mitigation: Define clear business rules for automated retry limits and human intervention triggers.

risks.risk: Unrealistic deadlines lead to rushed development and the omission of critical security controls.
risks.mitigation: Perform a phased rollout with a minimum viable secure product.

risks.risk: Generic compliance requirements lead to misinterpretation of specific RBI mandates, risking penalties.
risks.mitigation: Map requirements to specific RBI circular clauses and obtain legal sign-off.

risks.risk: Inadequate retention policies lead to data loss or illegal data hoarding, violating privacy laws.
risks.mitigation: Define specific retention periods per document type in the system configuration.

risks.risk: Lack of explicit consent mechanisms leads to severe legal penalties under data protection laws.
risks.mitigation: Implement a granular, auditable consent management module.

risks.risk: Failure to integrate real-time sanctions screening leads to onboarding prohibited entities.
risks.mitigation: Integrate with an automated, updated global sanctions database API.

risks.risk: Hard-coded logic prevents rapid updates to changing regulations, leading to compliance gaps.
risks.mitigation: Implement a rules engine for risk and compliance logic.

risks.risk: Over-reliance on automation without human oversight may lead to high false-rejection rates.
risks.mitigation: Implement a confidence-score threshold for automated approvals.

risks.risk: Unrestricted access to documents leads to internal data leaks or privacy violations.
risks.mitigation: Implement strict RBAC and audit logging for all document access.

risks.risk: Insecure API integration allows unauthorized account creation or data injection.
risks.mitigation: Implement mutual TLS and API gateway authentication.

risks.risk: Insecure resumption of onboarding could allow session hijacking or data tampering.
risks.mitigation: Require re-authentication for resuming abandoned sessions.

risks.risk: Undefined scope for the next quarter leads to scope creep and project failure.
risks.mitigation: Define a strict MVP scope and freeze requirements.

risks.risk: Inaccurate risk profiling allows high-risk entities to bypass AML controls.
risks.mitigation: Automate risk scoring based on predefined, auditable parameters.

risks.risk: Data misuse leads to regulatory fines and loss of customer trust.
risks.mitigation: Implement data tagging to restrict usage to KYC purposes only.

risks.risk: Expired KYC records lead to regulatory non-compliance and potential account freezing.
risks.mitigation: Automate notification workflows based on expiry dates.

risks.risk: Failure to detect unusual activity allows money laundering to occur undetected.
risks.mitigation: Implement real-time transaction monitoring with threshold-based alerts.

risks.risk: Delayed or improper STR filing leads to severe legal consequences for the bank.
risks.mitigation: Implement a dedicated, secure STR filing module with deadline tracking.

risks.risk: Failure to report breaches within legal deadlines results in heavy regulatory penalties.
risks.mitigation: Establish an automated incident response and notification workflow.

risks.risk: Inability to fulfill data subject requests leads to legal non-compliance.
risks.mitigation: Build a dedicated data management portal for customer requests.

risks.risk: Unencrypted data exposure leads to catastrophic data breaches.
risks.mitigation: Enforce AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit.

risks.risk: Unauthorized staff access to sensitive data leads to insider threats.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict RBAC and periodic audit log reviews.

risks.risk: Lack of liveness detection allows spoofing attacks using photos or deepfakes.
risks.mitigation: Integrate certified passive and active liveness detection solutions.

risks.risk: Exposure of PII in logs leads to data breaches in non-production environments.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated masking pipelines for all non-prod data.

risks.risk: Acceptance of forged documents leads to identity fraud.
risks.mitigation: Use automated document verification services with security feature detection.

risks.risk: Brute-force attacks on API endpoints lead to identity theft and system overload.
risks.mitigation: Implement rate limiting and IP-based throttling.

risks.risk: Tampering with audit trails hides fraudulent activity and prevents forensic investigation.
risks.mitigation: Use write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for audit logs.

risks.risk: Retaining data beyond legal limits increases liability and risk of data breach.
risks.mitigation: Automate data lifecycle management with purge triggers.

narrative.explanation: The Spiral model is the best fit because it excels at managing high technical uncertainty (4/5) and low requirement stability (1/5), where 88% of requirements remain vague. By utilizing iterative risk analysis, the model addresses the high consequence of failure (4/5) and regulatory criticality (4/5) while allowing the project to evolve despite the current lack of finality. The runner-up, Agile-DevSecOps hybrid, offers faster delivery cycles but lacks the structured risk-mitigation loops necessary for this project's significant regulatory and legacy-system dependencies.
tradeoffs: Increased overhead due to frequent risk assessment cycles.
Potential for slower initial velocity compared to pure Agile approaches.
Higher documentation burden required to satisfy regulatory audit trails.
would_change_if: If requirements stabilize and regulatory guidance is finalized, the Agile-V hybrid would become more efficient.
If the need for continuous delivery increases, the Agile-DevSecOps hybrid would overtake the Spiral model.
